evidence.field: 甲骨與金文字形、用例及讀音線索
evidence.text: The database interprets the early graph 从 as two 人 figures, one following the other, and reports ‘follow’ as its original sense. It reports oracle-bone uses for following and for ‘from’, including examples glossed ‘from the west’ and ‘from the east’; a bronze example is 宰椃角, ‘王格，宰椃从’. It says later 從 occurs with 彳 and sometimes 辵. For 從, its examples report bronze uses for accompanying and obeying, and a use通作 縱 meaning ‘indulge’. These are the database’s readings of cited inscriptions, not independent dating or visual readings of each inscription.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析: 从

evidence.source: 中央研究院, 漢字構形資料庫
evidence.text: The catalogue indexes a 從 oracle-bone example as 合集 29156, bronze examples as 集成 09105 and 10174, followed by Chu bamboo-and-silk forms and the 說文 small-seal form. Its account describes two 人, one ahead and one behind, and interprets the original sense as ‘follow’; it says 彳 or 辵 may be added. Catalogue identifiers and the entry’s account do not independently establish when semantic extensions arose.
evidence.title: 漢字「從」：字形演變

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, 異體字字典
evidence.field: 研訂說明 / 從 and 从
evidence.text: The editor reports that 說文 separates 从, glossed 相聽 and analyzed as 二人, from 從, glossed 隨從 and analyzed as 从 plus 辵, with 从 also described as phonetic. The editor considers ‘heed/obey’ and ‘follow/accompany’ semantically related by extension, and says oracle-bone texts use only 从; the separation into two Shuowen entries reflects later usage in this editorial account. The page also gives modern Mandarin readings zōng, zòng, cōng, cóng, while its cited Guangyun fanqie distinguish 疾容切 cóng, 七恭切 cōng, and 疾用切 zòng. These source analyses are not direct proof of every component’s early function.
evidence.title: [A01293-015] (從) — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The file is described as a digital vector depiction of 从 in Shang oracle script style. Its page identifies Sinica database image 42.F5EC as its source and states CC0 1.0/public-domain dedication for the file. This is a modern vector rendering of a historical script form, not a photograph of an oracle bone.

evidence.text: The Commons file description says this vector depicts 从 in bronze-script style and cites available character sources including Sinica and the CUHK database; its notes point to image B12581 on the 从 entry at hanziyuan.net. The file page states public-domain status for the modern vector rendering. This is a modern graphic reconstruction, not a photograph or rubbing of an inscribed bronze object.

search_audit.query: site:humanum.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/Lexis/lexi-mf 从 從 甲骨 金文; site:chardb.iis.sinica.edu.tw 從 字形演變 甲骨文; Wikimedia Commons 从 oracle bone script character 從 image
search_audit.outcome: Search performed; opened and inspected CUHK, Academia Sinica, and Taiwan MOE pages. CUHK supplied graph accounts, examples, and Shuowen quotation; Sinica supplied historical-form catalogue identifiers; MOE supplied its editorial distinction and phonetic entry analysis.

search_audit.query: site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File 从 oracle bone Chinese character; 从 字形 图片 Wikimedia Commons 从甲骨文
search_audit.outcome: Search performed; opened the oracle-script and seal-script file descriptions and inspected their stated historical style, source references, and reuse terms. Bronze candidate description was inspected on the Wiktionary-hosted file page, which presents Commons metadata. Direct image fetch for the oracle SVG returned HTTP 429, and a 從-bronze page attempt failed with cache miss; image pixels were not inspected.

gaps: No direct source in this research independently substantiated the proposed Tibetan etymologies or a graph-loan source word; no phonetic borrowing claim is adopted here.

The ancient 從 phonetic analysis is supported as Xu Shen’s account (and endorsed in the MOE editorial explanation), but no independent reconstructed pronunciations for both 从 and 從 were verified in this research. The dossier’s reconstruction data are imported metadata, not freshly checked external references.

The database reports oracle-bone ‘from’ uses and bronze uses for follow/accompany/obey/縱, but earliest securely dated attestations and the semantic links among these uses remain undetermined. No gloss-list chronology is inferred.

Sinica’s listed oracle-bone and bronze catalogue identifiers were inspected as page text; the underlying inscription images were not visually inspected. The Commons oracle vector fetch returned 429, and image pixels for the candidates were not inspected.

A Wikimedia Commons page for 從-bronze.svg failed with a cache-miss access error. Instead, the 从-bronze.svg file metadata page provided a usable candidate tied to a bronze style rendering, but its pixels were not checked.

items.period: Shang dynasty oracle script style; file uploaded 2011 and revised 2018
items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 从 in a Shang oracle-script form; the early graph is interpreted in specialist dictionary accounts as two people arranged one after another.
items.alt: Black line vector form of 从 in an oracle-script style, shown on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Shows the two-person graph associated with the early ‘follow’ interpretation. The Commons description identifies Sinica image 42.F5EC as its source; the underlying inscription and candidate pixels were not inspected in this research.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public-domain dedication stated on Commons for the vector rendering; underlying source image identified as Sinica database.

items.source_title: File:从-bronze.svg — Wiktionary file page drawing on Commons metadata
items.period: Bronze-script style; modern vector file dated 2011
items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 从 in a bronze-script style, illustrating the early graph used before or alongside forms expanded with movement components.
items.alt: Black line vector form of 从 in bronze-script style on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Pairs with the oracle-style candidate to show the graph in another historical script tradition. Metadata links it to the hanziyuan B12581 image and lists Sinica and CUHK references; pixels were not inspected.
items.rights: The file metadata states public-domain status for the modern vector representation; reuse rights should be checked on the Commons original file page before rendering.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; vector file uploaded 2011
items.caption: A modern vector rendering of 从 in a Shuowen seal-script style, allowing comparison with the earlier reported two-person form.
items.alt: Black line vector form of 从 in seal-script style on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Shows the later seal-script presentation cited in Commons metadata as hanziyuan S05944 and helps contextualize graphic regularization. It is a redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph; pixels were not inspected.
items.rights: Public domain dedication for the vector representation stated on Commons.

limitations.text: The proposed image URLs are image-file leads based on opened description pages. No candidate image pixels were visually inspected in this research; inscriptions are not represented as photographs unless separately established by the source page.

The bronze vector’s direct upload.wikimedia.org URL could not be established from the inspected metadata, so the image_url field is only a host-level lead and should not be treated as a verified direct file URL.
